deck: This week highlights significant funding rounds and strategic moves in space.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, emphasizing its role in co-orbital security and space domain awareness. With a valuation of $1.6 billion, the company is well-positioned to capitalize on increasing DoD interest in space security solutions. This funding follows a trend where defense priorities are driving substantial investments in space technology.
stories.soWhat: True Anomaly's success suggests that investors are betting on the military's growing reliance on space for operational security.

stories.head: Verde Technologies pivots to space solar panels
stories.body: Verde Technologies, known for its perovskite solar panels, is shifting its focus to the space sector, aiming to power satellites with its thin-film technology. This pivot could be a smart move as the demand for efficient energy solutions in space continues to rise. The company’s expertise in solar technology may give it a competitive edge in a crowded market.
stories.soWhat: If Verde can make this transition smoothly, it might just light the way for others looking to innovate in space energy solutions.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team up for SDA bid
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris are collaborating on a bid for a tactical Space Development Agency constellation, showcasing a strategic partnership aimed at enhancing U.S. space capabilities. This collaboration aligns with the recent $1.4 billion budget increase for space resilience in FY27, indicating a strong government push for improved satellite communications and defense infrastructure.
stories.soWhat: In defense, partnerships like this often mean shared risk—let's see if they can actually deliver on the promise.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Verde Technologies
watchlist.body: Their shift to space could attract attention from satellite manufacturers looking for efficient power solutions.

watchlist.title: Sybilla Technologies eyes U.S. expansion
watchlist.body: Their entry into the U.S. market may stir competition among existing players, particularly in satellite tech.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension could signal more government contracts on the horizon for data management solutions.

watchlist.title: Watch for hypersonic test updates
watchlist.body: The repeated delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests raise questions about the viability of these technologies moving forward.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
